1. Avant l’achat : bien préparer son pro: 1. Before buying: properly prepare your property project
Acheter un bien immobilier est une décis:
Buying property is an important decision that requires careful preparation. Before making an offer, it is essential to define your budget, taking into account not only the property price but also the various costs associated with the purchase. These include deed costs, registration duties or VAT depending on the type of property, as well as any financing-related costs. A clear assessment of your financial capacity helps avoid unpleasant surprises and allows you to look for a property suited to your circumstances.

It is also advisable to carefully check the characteristics of the property before committing. Its planning status, condition, any easements, co-ownership charges and certain administrative documents may have a significant impact on the purchase. The notary can assist the buyer with these checks and help explain the legal aspects of the transaction.
2. L’offre et le compromis de vente : de: 2. The offer and sale agreement: commitments to be taken seriously
Une fois le bien trouvé, l’acheteur peut:
Once the property has been found, the buyer may make an offer. This step should not be taken lightly: depending on its content and the circumstances, an offer may legally bind its author. It is therefore preferable to ensure that the main conditions of the purchase are clearly defined before signing it. Once the offer has been accepted, the parties may then enter into a sale agreement setting out the terms of the transaction.

The sale agreement is an essential step because it formalises the agreement between the seller and the buyer. It specifies, in particular, the price, the conditions of sale and any suspensive conditions, such as obtaining a mortgage loan. The notary then carries out the necessary checks and prepares the authentic deed. Although the agreement is sometimes referred to as a provisional sale agreement, it is not simply a temporary document: it represents an important commitment for both parties.
3. L’acte authentique : finaliser offici: 3. The authentic deed: officially finalising the purchase
Après la signature du compromis, plusieu:
After the sale agreement has been signed, several procedures are carried out before the authentic deed is signed. The notary conducts the necessary searches and checks to verify the legal and administrative status of the property and prepare the sale under the best possible conditions. This period also makes it possible to gather the required documents and, when the purchase is financed through a loan, coordinate the signing of the mortgage deed with the sale deed.

The signing of the authentic deed marks the completion of the transaction. The balance of the purchase price is paid and ownership is officially transferred to the buyer, subject to the terms set out in the deed. The notary also carries out the necessary formalities after signing. For the buyer, receiving support from the earliest stages therefore makes it possible to better understand their commitments, anticipate costs and secure their property project.
1. Le prix du bien ne représente pas le: 1. The property price does not represent the total cost of the purchase
Lorsqu’on prépare l’achat d’un logement:
When preparing to buy a home in Belgium, it is important not to focus solely on the price advertised by the seller. Several transaction-related costs must be added to this amount, some of which are unavoidable. The amount to budget for depends in particular on the Region where the property is located, its nature and the buyer’s circumstances. Anticipating these costs makes it possible to determine the budget more accurately and avoid unpleasant surprises at the time of signing.

The main costs include registration duties or, in certain circumstances, VAT. The applicable tax regime may vary depending on whether the property is an existing home or a new build, as well as on the buyer’s specific circumstances. It is therefore important to establish from the beginning of the project which tax regime applies to the intended purchase.
2. Les frais liés à l’acte notarié et au: 2. Costs related to the notarial deed and financing
L’acquisition d’un bien immobilier impli:
The purchase of a property also involves costs related to the notary’s involvement. These include the notary’s fees, as well as various administrative costs and disbursements required to complete the deed. The notary plays an essential role in legally securing the transaction and completing the formalities required to transfer ownership.

When the purchase is financed through a mortgage loan, the costs associated with the loan deed must also be taken into account. Depending on the circumstances, these may include certain duties, fees and administrative costs. These expenses are added to the cost of financing and should therefore be included in the overall budget calculation before making a commitment.
3. Comment bien anticiper son budget d’a: 3. How can you properly plan your purchase budget?
Avant de signer une offre ou un compromi:
Before signing an offer or sale agreement, it is advisable to prepare a complete estimate of the overall cost of the transaction. The property price, taxes, deed costs, any credit-related expenses and the costs required after the purchase should all be taken into account. A comprehensive view makes it possible to determine the actual amount required and, if necessary, adapt the property project.

The notary can assist the buyer with this preparation by helping them understand the costs associated with their project and the procedures to be completed. Since every situation is different, a personalised estimate is preferable to a simple general rule. Properly preparing the budget in advance therefore makes it possible to approach a property purchase with greater peace of mind and make an informed decision.
1. Préparer la vente et réunir les docum: 1. Preparing the sale and gathering the necessary documents
La vente d’un bien immobilier ne commenc:
The sale of a property does not begin on the day the deed is signed at the notary’s office. Several procedures must be completed beforehand to ensure that the property can be sold under the proper conditions. The seller must gather various documents concerning the property, its administrative and energy status and, in the case of an apartment, the co-ownership. This information gives the future buyer a clear understanding of the property before making a commitment.

The notary assists the seller with this preparation and carries out the necessary legal searches. In particular, the notary checks ownership of the property, any mortgages, easements or other matters that could affect the sale. This step makes it possible to identify potential difficulties early enough and prepare a secure transaction.
2. De l’offre au compromis de vente: 2. From the offer to the sale agreement
Une fois l’acquéreur trouvé, celui-ci pe:
Once a buyer has been found, they may make an offer to purchase. This step must be taken seriously, as an offer may have legal consequences depending on its terms and acceptance. It is therefore preferable to have its contents checked before making a commitment, particularly when specific conditions need to be included.

When the parties agree, they may sign a sale agreement. This document sets out the main conditions of the transaction: the identity of the parties, description of the property, price, payment terms and any suspensive conditions. The agreement represents an important commitment for both the seller and the buyer. The notary then continues the necessary checks in preparation for the authentic deed.
3. La signature de l’acte authentique et: 3. Signing the authentic deed and transferring ownership
Après le compromis, le notaire accomplit:
After the sale agreement, the notary completes the necessary formalities before the final signing. The notary checks the information relating to the property and ensures that the conditions required for the sale have been met. This period also allows the final documents to be prepared and the various administrative and financial aspects of the transaction to be settled.

The sale is officially completed when the authentic deed is signed. The price is paid according to the agreed terms and ownership is transferred to the buyer in accordance with the deed. The notary then completes the necessary formalities to ensure that the sale is enforceable against third parties. For the seller, this support helps secure every stage, from preparing the file to completing the transaction.
1. Comprendre ce qui se passe au moment: 1. Understanding what happens at the time of death
Lorsqu’un proche décède, sa succession s:
When a loved one dies, their estate is automatically opened. Their assets, including property, bank accounts, investments and potentially debts, must then be identified to determine what passes to the heirs. The first step is to establish who is entitled to inherit and to check whether the deceased left a will or other arrangements.

Heirs are not always required to accept the estate unconditionally. Depending on their circumstances, they may accept the inheritance, accept it under the benefit of inventory or renounce it. This decision deserves careful consideration, particularly when the deceased may have had debts. The notary can assist heirs throughout this process and help them understand the consequences of each option.
2. Identifier les biens, les dettes et l: 2. Identifying assets, debts and the heirs’ rights
Une succession peut comprendre des éléme:
An estate can include many different assets: a house or apartment, bank accounts, vehicles, investments, company shares or valuable possessions. It may also include loans or other debts. It is therefore necessary to establish a complete picture of the deceased’s assets and liabilities before distributing the estate among the heirs.

The notary may verify the legal status of assets, search for elements of the estate and determine each heir’s rights. When there are several heirs, the notary can also assist the parties in organising the distribution. The objective is to ensure that the transfer is as clear and secure as possible while taking into account legal provisions and any wishes expressed by the deceased.
3. Le règlement de la succession et les: 3. Settling the estate and inheritance taxes
Le règlement d’une succession implique é:
Settling an estate also involves tax obligations. Depending on the relevant Region and the heirs’ circumstances, inheritance tax may be due on the assets transferred. The amount depends in particular on the value of the assets received and the family relationship between the deceased and the heirs. It is therefore important to anticipate these aspects in order to understand the financial consequences of the inheritance.

The notary can assist heirs with the various formalities involved in settling the estate, including preparing the necessary documents and handling tax procedures. Since every estate is different, a personalised analysis is essential. Consulting a notary allows heirs to receive support during what is often a difficult period and settle the estate within a secure legal framework.
1. Anticiper pour mieux protéger son pat: 1. Planning ahead to better protect your assets
La constitution d’un patrimoine est souv:
Building wealth is often the result of many years of work, saving and investment. Yet the question of protecting and transferring that wealth is sometimes postponed. Planning ahead makes it possible to organise assets more effectively while taking family, professional and financial circumstances into account. Good estate planning allows you to consider what you wish to transfer, whom you wish to protect and the conditions under which the transfer should take place.

Since everyone’s circumstances are different, there is no single solution for protecting assets. The matrimonial regime, family composition, nature of the assets held and existence of a business can all have a significant influence on the choices to be considered. Notarial assistance makes it possible to analyse these different factors and establish an arrangement suited to each person’s objectives.
2. Donation, testament et autres outils: 2. Gifts, wills and other estate-planning tools
Plusieurs mécanismes peuvent être utilis:
Several mechanisms can be used to organise the transfer of assets. In certain circumstances, a gift can allow part of your assets to be transferred during your lifetime while establishing specific conditions. A will allows you to express your final wishes and organise the transfer of your assets in accordance with the applicable succession rules.

Other tools can also play a role in an estate-planning strategy, including a marriage contract or certain arrangements concerning ownership of assets. The choice of mechanism always depends on the individual’s circumstances and objectives. It is therefore important not to consider one solution in isolation, but rather the estate as a whole and the legal and tax consequences of the decisions being considered.
3. Préparer la transmission de son patri: 3. Preparing the transfer of your assets with a notary
Une planification patrimoniale efficace:
Effective estate planning is not only about transferring assets. It also aims to protect the interests of the person transferring the assets and anticipate potential difficulties between heirs. Preparing your estate in advance can help clarify your wishes, facilitate future procedures and, in certain situations, anticipate the tax consequences of the transfer.

A notary can assist with this planning at different stages of life and adapt solutions as circumstances change. Marriage, the birth of a child, the purchase of property, starting a business or a change in family circumstances can all be opportunities to review your estate planning. Planning your succession therefore means taking the time to consider the future and putting in place a framework that reflects your wishes.
1. Choisir la forme juridique adaptée à: 1. Choosing the legal structure suited to your project
Créer une entreprise est une étape impor:
Starting a business is an important step that requires several decisions before beginning operations. One of the first decisions concerns the choice of legal structure. In Belgium, the private limited company (SRL) is used by many entrepreneurs, but other types of companies may be considered depending on the project, the number of shareholders and the objectives pursued.

This choice should not be based solely on how easy the company is to establish. It can affect the liability of shareholders, the organisation of the company, project financing and governance. The notary can assist future shareholders in this process and help them establish a structure consistent with their business project.
2. Préparer les statuts et constituer la: 2. Preparing the articles of association and incorporating the company
Une fois la forme juridique choisie, plu:
Once the legal structure has been chosen, several procedures are required to incorporate the company. The future shareholders must define the rules governing its operation, including the distribution of shares, powers of directors, decision-making, shareholders’ rights and operating procedures. These elements are set out in the articles of association.

Where a notary’s involvement is required, the notary prepares the incorporation deed and ensures compliance with legal formalities. The notary can also draw the founders’ attention to important decisions that need to be made before incorporation. This stage is essential because the articles of association establish the legal framework in which the company will operate.
3. Après la constitution : donner vie à: 3. After incorporation: getting the business up and running
La signature de l’acte de constitution n:
Signing the incorporation deed does not mark the end of the process. After the company has been established, several formalities still need to be completed to allow the business to start operating under the right conditions. Depending on the project, these may include registration with the Crossroads Bank for Enterprises, VAT activation, opening a professional bank account or other procedures related to the business activity.

The notary’s role is not limited to incorporating the company. The notary can also assist entrepreneurs during important stages in the company’s life: amendments to the articles of association, the entry or exit of a shareholder, restructuring, transfer or dissolution. For an entrepreneur, obtaining legal support from the outset helps build a company on solid foundations and anticipate future developments.
